system: Tajika (Varshaphal, the yearly chart) - a separate system, not part of the Parashari knowledge base
sources: Balabhadra, Hayanaratna, tr. Martin Gansten, The Jewel of Annual Astrology (Brill 2020, open access; wisdomlib.org): the sixteen configurations, orbs of light, hadda table, five dignities and their points
Neelakantha, Tajika Neelakanthi (1587) as followed by B. V. Raman, Varshaphala or the Hindu Progressed Horoscope: five office-bearers, Tri-rashi lords, Sahams

Saham formulas are kept only where the classical texts agree; where Raman's table differs from Neelakanthi/Hayanaratna (Mitra, Asha, Vyapara and the night rule of some Sahams) the classical reading is used
policy: Sahams for matters the app does not read (see the v1.2 content policy) and those for imprisonment, illness and affliction are left out on purpose.
orb_rule: Two planets are within orbs when the gap is no more than half the sum of their orbs.
aspect_note: Tajika aspects go by sign: the 3rd/11th (sextile) and 5th/9th (trine) are friendly; the same sign, the 4th/10th (square) and the 7th (opposition) are inimical; the 2nd/12th and 6th/8th signs have no aspect.

dignity_points.uchcha: distance from the fall degree (under 180) divided by 9, at most 20
dignity_points.total: sum of the five divided by 4 (at most 20); under 5 weak, over 10 strong
dignity_points.relationship: Friend / neutral / enemy by Tajika aspect in the yearly chart: the sign lord in the 3rd, 5th, 9th or 11th sign from the planet is a friend, in the same, 4th, 7th or 10th an enemy, otherwise neutral (Hayanaratna 2.4).
dignity_points.check: Checked against a published Varshaphal report (Prokerala sample, 17 Feb 1990 10:00 Kottayam, years 2024 and 2025): Kshetra, Uchcha, Hadda, Drekkana and Navamsa points agree.

trirashi_note: Day / night lord of the Tri-rashi (triplicity) for the yearly ascendant.
varshesh_rules: The five office-bearers: lord of the birth ascendant, lord of the yearly ascendant, lord of the Muntha sign, the Tri-rashi lord and the day/night lord (lord of the Sun's sign by day, the Moon's sign by night).
The strongest of them by Pancha-vargiya bala that aspects the yearly ascendant (Tajika aspect) is the lord of the year.
If none aspects the ascendant, or all score under 5, the Muntha lord becomes the lord of the year.
The Moon is made lord of the year only when no other office-bearer aspects the ascendant.
saham_rule: Saham = A - B + C (by day). By night A and B swap unless the Saham is the same by day and night. Add 30 degrees when C does not fall between B and A counting forward through the zodiac.

yogas.Ikkavala: All seven planets are in angular or succedent houses (1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11): a year of rising fortunes; a feared difficulty tends to turn around.
yogas.Induvara: All seven planets are in cadent houses (3, 6, 9, 12): the year asks for patience; results come slowly.
yogas.Ithasala: The faster planet is behind the slower one in degrees, their signs aspect each other and the gap is within orbs: the matter is coming together.
yogas.Ishrafa: The faster planet has moved at least one degree past the slower one: the matter has peaked or is slipping away. Between benefics it is not harmful.
yogas.Nakta: The two significators do not aspect each other, but a faster planet in Ithasala with both carries the light between them: success through the help of another person.
yogas.Yamaya: The two significators do not aspect each other, but a slower planet in Ithasala with both carries the light: success through a counsellor or senior person.
yogas.Manau: The two significators are in Ithasala, but Mars or Saturn, slower than the faster of them, aspects it with an inimical aspect within its own orb: the promise is spoilt or delayed.
yogas.Kambool: The two significators are in Ithasala and the Moon is also in Ithasala with one or both: the matter is strongly supported.
yogas.Gairi-kambool: The two significators are in Ithasala, the Moon has no aspect to them but is in Ithasala with another planet from that planet's own or exaltation sign: support comes from outside.
yogas.Khallasara: The Moon is in no aspect or Ithasala with either significator: it weakens or cancels the promise.
yogas.Radda: A planet in the Ithasala is retrograde, combust or in the 6th, 8th or 12th house: the result is held back.
yogas.Duhphali-kuttha: The slower planet of an Ithasala is in its own or exaltation sign while the faster one has no dignity: still favourable.
yogas.Dutthottha-davira: Both significators are weak but in Ithasala: the matter is done with someone else's help.
yogas.Tambira: No Ithasala between the significators, but one of them, strong and at the end of a sign, applies to a strong planet in the next sign: very favourable.
yogas.Kuttha: A planet in its own or exaltation sign, in an angle or aspecting the ascendant, direct and not combust, and not aspected by Mars or Saturn: it gives its results in full.
yogas.Durupha: A planet that is retrograde, combust, in the 6th, 8th or 12th house, in the 7th sign from its own sign, or aspected by Mars or Saturn: it gives weak results.

hadda_note: Hadda (terms) as in Hayanaratna 2.5, except Aquarius, where Raman's Varshaphala order (Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, Mars, Saturn) is used: it is what the common Varshaphal software uses. Hayanaratna gives Mercury 7, Venus 6 there.
saham_judgement: A Saham does well when its ruler aspects it (Tajika aspect), sits in a good house and is strong, and is spoilt when its ruler sits in the 6th, 8th or 12th house, is combust or retrograde (Hayanaratna ch. 4; Raman). For the Sahams of strife and rivals a strong ruler means more of that matter, so they are shown as 'active' instead of 'supported'.
